text: In this activity, you are both rival designers for a book publisher. You will both be designing a cover for a new book, competing to see whose title and blurb will be chosen for the final book!

Before you Start:

Work together to decide which book you are designing the cover for. Here are some ideas:
  • A book you have both read
  • A TV series you have both watched
  • A film you have both seen
  • Something else!

Choose something you both know pretty well so you can imagine what the book might say inside. But don’t choose something with a cover you remember, otherwise you might accidentally copy the original!

What to Do:

The winner will be the person who comes up with the best title and blurb for the book. You can design the pictures and layout if you want, but don’t forget that the competition is all about the words!

  1. On a piece of paper, write a new title for the book.
    • Don’t use the original title.
    • Think carefully what the book is about and make sure the title fits.
    • Keep it quite short so it is easy to see.
    • Try and make it interesting or exciting so that it makes someone want to read the book.
  2. Below the title, write a new blurb for the book.
    • A blurb is usually between 100 and 200 words long. Try to stick to this!
    • Remember that a blurb is trying to tempt someone to read the book – it should make the person want to read more.
    • The blurb needs to show what is in the book without giving too much away – it would be rubbish if the blurb told you the ending!
    • Make sure the blurb matches the tone of the book – if the book is exciting, it needs to be exciting, but if the book is a serious non-fiction text, you might need something more serious.
  3. When you have finished, read through and check you work. You might decide to make some changes and improvements.
  4. When you have both finished, read each other’s title and blurb. Talk together about what you like and compare what you have both written. Which will win? Why?
